dailyInsight.headline: Audit agent diagnostics for signed URLs before widening egress
dailyInsight.insight: OpenClaw's fresh redaction change supports one bounded audit for teams operating agent tools: inspect the diagnostic paths that may serialize URL query strings and form-like request bodies before treating those logs as safe to retain or share. The public patch adds signed URL and X-prefixed authorization names to the redaction machinery and tests both network-policy and logging paths.
dailyInsight.mechanism: The change moves URL credential masking toward shared query-pair classification, recognizes sig and X-prefixed authorization fields, and applies the same sensitive-key decision to URL, body, and diagnostic representations. The focused tests are evidence that these input shapes were considered; they are not proof that every plugin, proxy, exporter, or downstream log store is covered.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: Agent systems increasingly carry browser destinations, storage links, provider calls, and gateway headers through support and observability channels. A secret that is protected at the request boundary can still leak when a URL or payload is rendered for debugging. Auditing the representations is a reversible way to find a gap before a broad egress or logging rollout makes it durable.

actions.audience: Agent-harness operator or integrator who retains HTTP diagnostics
actions.label: Run one redaction fixture drill
actions.instruction: In a disposable test log pipeline, send representative signed URLs and diagnostic bodies using sig and X-prefixed authorization fields. Check the application log, error reporter, proxy trace, and exported support bundle for the literal values. Add a regression fixture for every representation that can preserve the request, and keep production credentials out of the drill.

receipts.title: fix(net-policy): redact sig and x-* auth params in URLs and bodies (#116957)
receipts.supports: Shows the fresh source-level redaction changes and tests for signed URL parameters, X-prefixed authorization material, URL query pairs, and diagnostic-body handling.

confidence.basis: One fresh, directly inspected OpenClaw commit changes both the shared redaction implementation and focused tests for the diagnostic representations described in this audit.

dailyInsight.limitation: This is source-level evidence from OpenClaw. It does not establish a released build, coverage of every plugin or log exporter, safe retention policies, or that another agent stack uses the same redaction paths.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise this call if a public regression shows the same sig or X-prefixed values survive a covered URL or body path, if the project documents an intentionally unmasked representation, or if the implementation moves the responsibility to a boundary that does not receive diagnostics.
dailyInsight.watchNext: Watch for end-to-end fixtures covering proxy, telemetry, error-reporting, and plugin exports, where redaction failures tend to reappear after an application-level log is fixed.
